correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the exact stages after setting U=(sqrt(r),0) by rotational equivariance. With t=h(a+br), q=br/(a+br), and s=t^2, the normalized second-stage frequency is B=1+qs/4 and the third-stage coordinates are (1-sB/2,-tB). Its normalized frequency is C=1+q[-sB+sB^2+s^2B^2/4]. Expanding X=1-sB(1+C)/4 and -Y/t=(1+2B+C(1-sB/2))/4 in X^2+Y^2 gives zero coefficients at s,s^2; the s^3,s^4,s^5 coefficients are (q+1)^2/64, -q(q+1)(2q+1)/128, q(9q+8)/1024. Evenness follows directly from X even and Y odd in t. Thus the generic r-increment is r(a+br)^4(a+2br)^2 h^6/64, and its unique nonstationary positive-radius cancellation q=-1 leaves r_star H^10/1024. Energy is r/2, so actual energy defects are half the radial increments; these are local errors of orders five and nine in the stated convention, not orders of the full state method. If a+br=0 all stages vanish. In the bounded layer r/r_star=1+H^2 y the three displayed polynomial coefficients contribute H^10 times y^2/16, y/64, 1/1024, respectively; omitted terms are uniformly O(H^12) since the denominator stays away from zero. Dividing by H^2 gives an Euler recurrence of step H^8 with O(H^10) residual. The exact Riccati solution is tau/(1024-8 tau); on every compact pre-pole interval the bounded Lipschitz Euler comparison accumulates O_T(H^2) and closes the bounded-layer bootstrap. Physical time scales as h^-7, with no claim of a discrete blow-up or accuracy at the pole. Inspected frozen verify.py and VERIFICATION.md but did not run the submitted code; the coefficient and uniform-error reasoning were checked analytically, not inferred from the floating-point demonstrations.

value.rationale: The radius is selected by an intrinsic zero of the generic drift, not an arbitrary convenient test amplitude. At that zero the order gain and its lifetime are different questions: the error drives the orbit off the exceptional amplitude, and the matched detuning law gives a quantitative duration and shape of that departure. This is a meaningful invariant-accuracy diagnostic for a known integrator and a natural oscillator, beyond recomputing a generic order coefficient.
